# Qirsh — AdMob production readiness

**2026-09-03.** Audited against the actual implementation, not against plans.
**Nothing is enabled. No production ad traffic has been or can be generated by
any build in this repository.**

---

## 1. THE DECISION YOU HAVE TO MAKE FIRST

The repository contains an owner strategy document that **prohibits the feature
that was later commissioned**. This surfaced during review and it outranks any
recommendation I or the reviewers could make.

`docs/plans/MONETIZATION_PLAN.md` (2026-06-14) says, in a numbered list of
product principles:

> **6. Offers are in their own section.** Dashboard, transactions, and budgets
> are completely **ad-free**.

and, in its format section:

> **❌ Banner Ads — Never** — "Destroys the premium feel. Distracts during
> financial review. CPM is low — not worth the trust damage."
> **❌ Interstitials — Never** — "Full stop. No exceptions for a financial app."
> **NEVER: Banner ads, interstitials, selling user data, sweepstakes…**

**Both shipped ad formats contradict that document**: the report-export
interstitial (commissioned as R4/R7) and the transactions banner (commissioned
2026-09-01, placement delegated to the reviewers).

This is the same pattern as `ANDROID_SMS_CAPTURE_DECISION.md`, which said SMS
capture was disabled long after you had revoked that position — an older
document that a later decision superseded and nobody revised.

**What I did NOT do:** silently delete the placement, and silently keep it.
Either would be me resolving a product question that is yours. Instead:

- The banner is **fully implemented, reviewed and inert** — three separate
  owner actions are required before it can appear (two flags plus production ad
  units), so nothing ships against your principles by accident.
- The conflict is recorded here, at the top, where the next session will see it.

**Three ways forward, and my recommendation:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **A. Supersede principle 6** for transactions only, as you did for SMS capture. One line in `MONETIZATION_PLAN.md`. Everything is then ready. |
| **B. Keep principle 6, move the banner.** But the only remaining non-excluded surface is Coupons, and **both reviewers independently said keep AdMob out of Coupons** — a third-party banner competing with your own affiliate marketplace. There is effectively nowhere else. |
| **C. Keep principle 6, ship no banner.** The infrastructure stays dormant; the interstitial keeps its own separate decision. |

**My recommendation: A or C, not B.** The plan is 3 months old and predates both
commissions; if you still believe principle 6, C is honest and costs only the
banner. B is the worst of both — it puts ads exactly where your own reviewers
said not to.

## 2. What is actually implemented

**Banner placements: exactly ONE.** `grep -rn "QirshAdBanner" app/lib` outside
`features/ads/` returns a single call site.

| | |
|---|---|
| Placement | `AdPlacement.transactionsList` — the only enum value |
| Call site | `transactions_screen.dart`, guarded by `itemIndex == 0 && !pendingOnly && sections.length > 1` |
| Meaning | after the first complete date section, never on the pending-review filter, never when it would be the last element |

**Interstitial placements: exactly ONE.** Report export
(`reports_screen.dart:74`), preloaded from `app_shell.dart:393`.

**Excluded — by construction, not by list.** A guard test asserts that
`QirshAdBanner` appears at exactly one allowlisted path. Every other screen is
therefore excluded automatically, including every one added in future:
onboarding, auth, SMS capture and permission, Smart Inbox, capture review,
transaction detail, add/edit transaction, all confirmation and destructive
dialogs, account deletion, privacy and consent surfaces, backup/restore, data
transfer, budget and goal editors, card and account detail, error and empty
states, force-update, savings confirm sheet, savings breakdown, merchant offer
detail, and all Coupons screens.

## 3. Configuration state

| Item | State |
|---|---|
| Android App ID | manifest `${admobAppId}`; Gradle resolves `ADMOB_APP_ID_ANDROID`, validates the shape, and **throws GradleException** on a malformed value or the test publisher in a release |
| iOS App ID | `GADApplicationIdentifier = $(ADMOB_APP_ID)`; Release maps to `$(ADMOB_APP_ID_IOS)` |
| Build inputs | **six**, in one file, guard-asserted: `ADMOB_APP_ID_{IOS,ANDROID}`, `ADMOB_INTERSTITIAL_{IOS,ANDROID}`, `ADMOB_BANNER_{IOS,ANDROID}` |
| Debug/profile | **always Google TEST units.** Verified in the built APK: `ca-app-pub-3940256099942544~…` |
| Release | production values required and shape-checked; a release resolving to the test publisher returns **null** → no ads, never a silent fallback |
| `SKAdNetworkItems` | one entry (`cstr6suwn9.skadnetwork`) — **identical to the google_mobile_ads 9.0.0 example plist**. Longer lists are for mediation partners; Qirsh uses none. See §6 |
| ATT | **no** `NSUserTrackingUsageDescription`, no prompt. Every request sets `nonPersonalizedAds: true` + legacy `npa` |
| `ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID` | auto-merged by the SDK into the APK — **must appear in Play Data Safety** |
| `app-ads.txt` | **automated**: `tools/build_legal_site.py` emits it at the domain root from `ADMOB_PUBLISHER_ID`, validates the shape, and **refuses to write a placeholder** |
| Flags | `enable_banner_ads` and `enable_banner_transactions_list`, both **false**; `enable_report_ads` **false** |

## 4. Consent and ad-free

**UMP is the sole authority.** No Qirsh-owned advertising-consent boolean exists
anywhere — a guard bans the symbol. Consent is gathered once per session from
`AppShell`, for **either** ads product (a bug fixed earlier: it used to check
only the report flag, so a banners-on/report-off release would never have
gathered consent).

**Ad-free entitlement is server-authoritative and three-state.**
`verifiedActive` → no ad. `verifiedInactive` → eligible. `unknownOrStale` — any
timeout, unreachable server, malformed response or stale cache → **no ad**.
Never "not entitled".

**Ten gates**, all of which must pass, and gates 1–5 resolve *before the widget
is inserted*: two flags, complete build config, entitlement, UMP consent,
`Visibility.of` (the shell is an `IndexedStack` whose hidden children stay laid
out), route currency, no open modal (`AdWidget` is a platform view and this app
has real platform-view-over-sheet history), width ≥ 320, and a 30s per-placement
throttle held statically so it survives the unmount a tab switch causes.

---

## 5. Defects found in this review and fixed

Both reviewers ran independently. Four real defects, all now fixed and tested.

1. **Entitlement and consent were cached for the process lifetime.** Both were
   plain `FutureProvider`s that nothing ever invalidated. A user who **earned
   ad-free mid-session kept seeing banners until restart** — breaking the single
   promise this gate exists to keep — and a first evaluation that raced UMP
   cached "no consent" for the whole session. Now `autoDispose`, and invalidated
   on the consent/resume path. *Both reviewers found this independently.*
2. **The adaptive size was thrown away.** The loader resolved a real
   `AnchoredAdaptiveBannerAdSize` and then rebuilt `AdSize(width, height)` from
   its numbers, which makes the request a **custom** size — different, thinner
   inventory. The resolved object is now passed through, and the null fallback
   is the genuine `AdSize.banner` rather than `width × 50`. *Both reviewers.*
3. **Ineligibility did not release a held ad.** Only the *visual* gate disposed;
   when entitlement or consent turned false the widget returned an empty box and
   kept the loaded ad alive. Now both paths tear down. *Codex.* Pinned by a test
   proven non-vacuous.
4. **No tap shield on insertion.** Insert-when-loaded shifts content down once,
   and a finger already descending toward a transaction row could land on the
   ad — the accidental-click category Google actually penalises. Taps are now
   ignored for 800 ms after the slot appears. *Fable.*

**Where the reviewers disagreed:** placement. One said the transactions banner
is right; the other said remove it and cited `MONETIZATION_PLAN.md`. Verified —
the citation is real, and it is why §1 exists. Repository evidence beat both
opinions.

## 6. Exact AdMob Console actions required from you

None of this was done. **Do not enable production ads without explicit
activation authorization.**

1. **Create the AdMob app** for `com.youssefsafwat.mali` (and the iOS bundle).
   → gives `ADMOB_APP_ID_ANDROID`, `ADMOB_APP_ID_IOS`.
2. **Create two banner ad units** → `ADMOB_BANNER_ANDROID`, `ADMOB_BANNER_IOS`.
3. **Create two interstitial ad units** → `ADMOB_INTERSTITIAL_ANDROID`,
   `ADMOB_INTERSTITIAL_IOS`.
4. **Set the banner refresh interval** in the console. The client has **no
   refresh timer by design**, so the console setting is the only refresh — and a
   conservative interval also limits invalid-traffic exposure.
5. **Publish `app-ads.txt`**: run
   `ADMOB_PUBLISHER_ID=pub-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX python3 tools/build_legal_site.py`
   and deploy. AdMob restricts serving to newly configured apps without it.
6. **Consider the SKAdNetwork list.** Ours matches the SDK's own example. If you
   ever enable mediation, paste Google's then-current partner list into
   `ios/Runner/Info.plist`.
7. **Play Data Safety**: declare `ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID`; ads are
   non-personalized and no financial data is used for targeting.
8. **App Store privacy**: declare the SDK's data collection; no ATT prompt is
   needed because nothing requests IDFA.

Supply the six IDs as build-time values — **never commit them**. A guard fails
the build if any `ca-app-pub-` literal other than Google's test publisher appears
in `lib/`.
